report.summary: The change splits Worker/UI/component test tasks and fixture builds into separate Turbo cache entries with transit hashing, adds a fail-closed docs-only CI path, makes many Worker RPC/op test groups concurrent, and narrows phone browser coverage. Most of it checks out: the classifier falls back to the full suite for missing, invalid or unreachable bases, empty diffs and both sides of renames; the required check job always runs; Turbo inputs match the real import graph (Worker tests never import src/ui or src/routes; fixtures only import src and their own folders; Vite outputs match the cached outputs); and Held fakes now clean up per test. One blocking problem: the newly concurrent 'step runner rules' group contains a case that changes the module-global STEP_LIMITS table, so every case running beside it gets a 300 ms settings.read timeout. On a busy runner a neighbour's settings.read can be skipped, its setup script never starts, and the case times out.

findings.text: The 'step runner rules' group is now describe.concurrent (maxConcurrency 4), but its 'aborts a step at its timeout' case changes the module-global STEP_LIMITS table that the WorkspaceDO reads through limitOf(). While it runs, every other case in the group also gets a 300 ms settings.read timeout instead of 10 s. Keep this group sequential, or move the timeout case into a sequential group. This breaks the AGENTS.md rule the same change adds about keeping global-state groups sequential.

evidence.why: STEP_LIMITS is exported from src/do/workspace/runner.ts and read at step time through `limitOf = (step) => STEP_LIMITS[step] ?? DEFAULT_LIMIT`. With `describe.concurrent("step runner rules"...)`, the neighbouring cases 'recovery after a DO restart: a running op that waits...' and 'a step's timing includes the time it waited...' seed with `effective: settingsWith({ scripts: { setup: "npm ci" } })`, which reaches the workspace only through the fake's settings.read handler. If that request takes over 300 ms on a busy runner, settings.read fails 3 times and is skipped (03 Step limits: 'skip'). Defaults are used, no setup script exists, and `drive(... requestsOf("script.start").length === 1 ...)` never succeeds, so the case times out. This is a shared global under concurrent cases.

findings.text: The docs-only path runs oxlint and oxfmt through `bunx --package <tool>@<pinned devDependency version>` with no node_modules. The .oxlintrc.json and .oxfmtrc.json configs use only built-in plugins, so this should work, but neither the lightweight path nor the git fetch-by-SHA in ci-changes.test.ts was executed here (running the test needed approval). A first docs-only CI run would confirm it.

checked.risk: Real contracts: Turbo transit nodes, Vite default outDir and cached outputs, Playwright device and tap contracts, GitHub Actions event SHAs and checkout depth

Failure paths: the classifier fails closed when the base is missing, all zeros, invalid or unreachable, when the diff is empty, and when a git command fails or times out; ci.ts budget and exit handling in docs-only mode
Cache correctness: Worker, UI and component inputs against the real import graph, fixture-build inputs including tailwind @source and imports, globalDependencies
Tests: shared spies, globals and cleanup under the new describe.concurrent groups; distinct fixtures per case; per-test hold cleanup
Security and build environment: no secrets touched; the docs-only path uses pinned tool versions from package.json; no workflow path ignores; required check kept
Spec and repo rules: CI docs and Build Plan updated in the same change; AGENTS.md rules compared with the implementation; no code or config reads docs/ or spikes/ files
Browser test coverage changes: phone project grep and tags, tap() requires hasTouch (iPhone 13 device), removed setViewportSize
